ops.title: Core plan contract: materialization tokens can collide with user config strings — escape or namespace them
ops.description:
Refuter-confirmed during the 0.9.0 oracle-inversion review (both hosts affected; pre-existing in Go since 0.8.0, inherited by Python in 0.9.0). The plan op's argv carries `${file:<id>}` and `${isolated_config_dir}` placeholder tokens in the same namespace as arbitrary user configuration: a `ClaudeConfig.system_prompt` that IS exactly `${file:stdout}` gets rewritten to the minted stdout temp path (hosts substitute by exact argv-element equality), and any config string CONTAINING the literal `${isolated_config_dir}` gets rewritten inside isolated claude runs (hosts substitute by substring across argv + env values). The retired hand-written Python passed such strings through verbatim.

Fix is CORE-FIRST and cross-host: change the plan contract so tokens can't collide with user data (e.g. carry placeholder positions out-of-band as (argv_index, span) references, or emit argv as tagged segments), regenerate vectors (`cargo run -p conformance-gen -- --write`), and update BOTH hosts' materialization (go/exec.go + spawnllm/backends/base.py invocation/env) in the same PR. Pathological inputs only — no realistic config carries these literals — hence P2/backlog.

ops.text: a config string equal to or containing a placeholder token survives planning + materialization verbatim in Python and Go
vectors regenerated; strict conformance + all three replays green
